scenario: 面试官问「你会怎么算这个模型要用的特征」,想看你有没有把特征计算当成一条可选择的谱系,而不是默认全走实时。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks how you'd compute the model's features, watching whether you treat feature computation as a spectrum rather than defaulting to real-time everything.
q: 特征计算的三种范式(批/流/请求时)本质上在权衡哪三件事？
q_en: What three things do the batch/streaming/request-time paradigms fundamentally trade off?
why: 特征计算是一条「新鲜度 vs 成本 vs 复杂度」的谱系:越新鲜的特征越贵、运维越难。强答案会把范式选择绑到新鲜度要求、延迟预算、成本和特征可得性上,而不是一句「全部实时」。
why_en: Feature computation is a freshness-versus-cost-versus-complexity spectrum where fresher features cost more and are harder to operate, so tie the choice to the freshness requirement, not a blanket real-time answer.
diagram:
flowchart LR B["批处理
小时级 · 最便宜"] --> S["流处理
秒-分钟级 · 中"] S --> R["请求时
毫秒级 · 最贵"] B -.越往右越新鲜/越贵/越难运维.-> R
options: 模型精度 vs 训练时长 vs 参数量——特征管线只影响离线训练效果
存储格式 vs 压缩率 vs 网络带宽——本质是一个数据序列化问题
新鲜度 vs 成本 vs 复杂度——越新鲜越贵越难运维,选择要绑到延迟预算和特征可得性
模型大小 vs GPU 数量 vs 电费——本质是硬件采购问题
options_en: Model accuracy vs training time vs parameter count — feature pipelines only affect offline training quality.
Storage format vs compression ratio vs network bandwidth — fundamentally a serialization problem.
Freshness vs cost vs complexity — fresher is pricier and harder to operate, so tie the choice to latency budget and feature availability.
Model size vs GPU count vs electricity bill — fundamentally a hardware-procurement problem.
optionExplanations: 范式差别在特征新鲜度和服务路径成本,不是训练时长或参数量,这几项跟批/流/请求时的选择无关。
序列化是实现细节;真正的取舍是「特征要多新鲜、愿意为此付多少成本和运维」。
对;三范式沿新鲜度轴排开,新鲜度越高成本和复杂度越高,选谁由延迟预算和特征能否预算好决定。
硬件采购是下游结果;先要决定的是特征新鲜度档位,而不是买几张卡。
optionExplanations_en: The paradigms differ on feature freshness and serving-path cost, not training time or parameter count, which are unrelated to the batch/streaming/request-time choice.
Serialization is an implementation detail; the real tradeoff is how fresh features must be and what cost and ops you'll pay for it.
Correct — the three paradigms line up along a freshness axis where higher freshness means higher cost and complexity, chosen by latency budget and availability.
Hardware procurement is a downstream consequence; you first decide the freshness tier, not how many cards to buy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 特征反映现实的实时程度;批处理小时级、流处理秒-分钟级、请求时毫秒级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feature freshness is how up-to-date a feature is: hours for batch, seconds-to-minutes for streaming, milliseconds for request-time.

termDefinitions.term: training-serving skew / 训练-服务偏斜
termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时算特征的逻辑与线上服务时不一致,导致线上表现掉点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Training-serving skew is when the feature logic at training time differs from serving time, degrading online performance.

scenario: 要给推荐模型算「用户过去 30 天购买次数、平均会话时长、用户 embedding」,这些口味类信号变化很慢,数据量上亿条。
scenario_en: You need a recommender's features like 30-day purchase counts, average session duration, and user embeddings — taste signals that change slowly over 100M+ records.
q: 这类变化缓慢的大规模聚合特征,该用哪种管线算？
q_en: Which pipeline should compute these slowly-changing large-scale aggregate features?
why: 口味/长周期聚合几小时甚至一天不更新也没关系,批处理最便宜(spot 实例)、最好调试(有界数据可回放/单测),正好匹配「新鲜度要求宽松」。批处理的代价是最新只到上次跑批的时刻。
why_en: Slowly-changing aggregates tolerate hours of staleness, so batch is cheapest and easiest to debug, matching a relaxed freshness requirement at the cost of being only as fresh as the last run.
tradeoff: 批处理(最便宜、可回放、但小时级陈旧) vs 流/请求时(更新鲜但更贵更难)
options: 批处理:口味变化慢,几小时陈旧可接受,用 Spark 跑上亿条最便宜也最好调试
请求时同步计算:在预测请求里现算 30 天购买次数,保证绝对最新
流处理:为 30 天聚合维护一个永不关闭的有状态窗口,持续实时更新
干脆不预计算,每次训练和推理都全表扫描一遍历史订单
options_en: Batch: taste changes slowly and hours of staleness is fine, so run Spark over 100M+ records at the lowest cost and easiest debugging.
Request-time synchronous compute: recompute the 30-day purchase count inside each prediction request to guarantee absolute freshness.
Streaming: keep a never-closing stateful window for the 30-day aggregate, updating continuously in real time.
Skip precomputation entirely and full-scan the order history on every training and inference call.
whenOtherWins: 若这个聚合窗口缩到「最近 10 分钟」并要驱动实时决策(如反欺诈),批处理的小时级陈旧就不够,应改用流处理的有状态窗口。
whenOtherWins_en: If the window shrinks to the last 10 minutes and must drive real-time decisions like fraud, batch's hourly staleness is too stale and a streaming stateful window wins.
optionExplanations: 对;宽松新鲜度 + 大数据量正是批处理的主场,spot 实例最便宜、有界输入可回放可单测。
在服务路径里现算 30 天聚合会顶破单请求延迟预算,而且这类特征根本不需要毫秒新鲜。
为一个 30 天窗口常驻有状态流是杀鸡用牛刀:always-on 成本和状态运维都白付,新鲜度还用不上。
每次全表扫上亿条订单既慢又贵,预计算存下来就是为了避免重复扫描。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — relaxed freshness plus big data is batch's home turf: spot instances are cheapest and the bounded input is replayable and unit-testable.
Computing a 30-day aggregate inside the serving path blows the per-request latency budget, and these features don't need millisecond freshness.
A resident stateful stream for a 30-day window is overkill: you pay always-on cost and state ops for freshness you never use.
Full-scanning 100M+ orders every call is slow and costly; precomputing exists precisely to avoid re-scanning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式批处理引擎,一个 job 就能在上亿条历史数据上算聚合特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Spark is a distributed batch engine that can compute aggregate features over 100M+ historical records in one job.

termDefinitions.meaning: 云厂商随时可回收的廉价算力,适合可重跑的批任务,大幅降本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Spot/preemptible instances are cheap, reclaimable cloud compute ideal for rerunnable batch jobs, cutting cost sharply.

scenario: 面试官追问:批处理特征管线除了便宜,还有哪些运维上的好处让它成为默认起点。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks what operational advantages, beyond cost, make batch the default starting point for feature pipelines.
q: 批处理管线有哪些「有界数据」带来的运维优势？(多选)
q_en: Which operational advantages come from batch's bounded datasets? (multiple)
why: 批处理跑在有界的历史快照上:输入固定 → 输出确定,可重放同一份输入拿到同样结果,方便回填、单测和调试;而且没有需要重建的运行时状态。代价只是新鲜度停在上次跑批。
why_en: Batch runs on a bounded historical snapshot, so the same input deterministically reproduces the same output, making backfill, unit testing, and debugging easy with no runtime state to reconstruct.
options: 有界输入 → 输出确定,重放同一份数据得到同样结果
容易回填历史(backfill)和写单元测试
没有需要在故障后重建的运行时状态
特征天然是毫秒级新鲜的
options_en: Bounded input means deterministic output — replaying the same data yields the same result.
Easy to backfill history and write unit tests.
No runtime state that must be reconstructed after a failure.
Features are inherently millisecond-fresh.
optionExplanations: 对;有界 + 确定性让「重跑一遍」永远得到相同结果,是批处理好调试的根本。
对;历史数据摆在那里,想补哪段跑哪段,也能拿固定输入断言输出做单测。
对;批任务是无状态地扫一遍输入,挂了重跑即可,不像流要恢复窗口状态。
错;批处理恰恰最不新鲜,只到上次跑批的时刻,毫秒新鲜是请求时范式的特征。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — bounded plus deterministic means a rerun always reproduces the same result, the root of batch's debuggability.
Correct — history sits there so you can recompute any slice, and fixed inputs let you assert outputs in unit tests.
Correct — a batch job statelessly scans its input and just reruns on failure, unlike streaming which must recover window state.
Wrong — batch is the least fresh, only current to the last run; millisecond freshness belongs to request-time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对历史时间段重新计算特征;批处理因输入有界最容易做。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backfill recomputes features over past time ranges; batch makes this easiest because its input is bounded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一份输入必然得到同一份输出,便于调试与回放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Deterministic output means the same input always yields the same output, aiding debugging and replay.

scenario: 一条特征用「每天凌晨跑一次」的批 job 计算,产品团队问它能有多新鲜。
scenario_en: A feature is computed by a batch job that runs once nightly; the product team asks how fresh it can be.
q: 日频批 job 算出的特征,新鲜度上限是多少,这对哪些场景是硬伤？
q_en: What's the freshness ceiling of a daily batch job, and which use cases does it break?
why: 新鲜度上限 = 跑批间隔:日频最坏能陈旧到接近 24 小时(下一次跑批前一直用旧值)。对反欺诈、会话内特征这种分钟级需求是硬伤;对内容推荐、信用评分这种慢变量则完全够用。
why_en: The freshness ceiling equals the run interval, so a daily job can be nearly 24 hours stale, which breaks minute-scale needs like fraud but is fine for slow signals like content recs.
options: 上限约 1 秒陈旧,足以驱动反欺诈系统的分钟级滑动窗口计数与实时拦截
上限约 24 小时陈旧(等于跑批间隔),对分钟级反欺诈/会话特征是硬伤,对慢变量够用
上限约 5 分钟陈旧,和流处理的持续物化几乎等价,可支撑会话内特征更新
没有陈旧,批 job 会在源数据一有变化就自动触发重算,始终保持最新
options_en: Ceiling of about 1 second stale, enough to drive a fraud system's minute-scale sliding-window counts and real-time blocking.
Ceiling of about 24 hours stale (equal to the run interval), a dealbreaker for minute-scale fraud/session features but fine for slow signals.
Ceiling of about 5 minutes stale, nearly equivalent to streaming's continuous materialization and able to support in-session features.
No staleness — a batch job auto-recomputes the moment source data changes, always staying current.
optionExplanations: 1 秒新鲜要常驻流/请求时才做得到,日频批根本达不到,分钟级反欺诈也不能靠它。
对;新鲜度上限就等于跑批周期,日频最坏近 24h 陈旧,慢变量够、分钟级需求不够。
5 分钟是流处理量级;日频批相差好几个数量级,不能画等号。
批 job 只在被调度时跑,数据变化不会触发重算,天生带跑批间隔的陈旧。
optionExplanations_en: One-second freshness needs a resident stream or request-time; a daily batch can't reach it and can't back minute-scale fraud.
Correct — the freshness ceiling equals the run cadence, so daily is up to ~24h stale: fine for slow signals, not for minute-scale needs.
Five minutes is streaming territory; a daily batch is orders of magnitude off, so they're not equivalent.
A batch job only runs when scheduled; data changes don't trigger recompute, so run-interval staleness is inherent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 批 job 特征最新只能到上次跑批时刻,上限等于跑批间隔。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The freshness ceiling of a batch feature is the last run time, so the ceiling equals the run interval.

scenario: 把批处理、流处理、请求时实时三种范式放在同一张决策矩阵上,准备在面试里一眼说清取舍。
scenario_en: Placing batch, streaming, and request-time real-time on one decision matrix to explain the tradeoffs at a glance in an interview.
q: 沿「新鲜度、吞吐、成本」轴,三范式的排序大致是怎样的？
q_en: Along freshness, throughput, and cost, how do the three paradigms roughly rank?
why: 新鲜度:批(小时)< 流(秒-分钟)< 请求时(毫秒);吞吐:批/流高、请求时低(逐请求);成本:批最低、请求时最高、流居中。记这条单调关系就能快速匹配需求。
why_en: Freshness rises batch < streaming < request-time, throughput is high for batch/streaming but low per-request for request-time, and cost is lowest for batch and highest for request-time.
tradeoff: 新鲜度越高(批→流→请求时)成本和复杂度越高、单点吞吐越低
options: 三范式新鲜度、成本都一样,只是所用工具名字不同
请求时新鲜度最低、成本最低,批处理新鲜度最高、成本最高
新鲜度批<流<请求时,成本也随之批<流<请求时,吞吐请求时最低
流处理在三项上都严格优于批和请求时,是永远的最优解
options_en: All three have identical freshness and cost; only the tool names differ.
Request-time has the lowest freshness and cost, while batch has the highest freshness and cost.
Freshness rises batch < streaming < request-time, cost rises the same way, and request-time has the lowest throughput.
Streaming strictly dominates batch and request-time on all three axes and is always optimal.
optionExplanations: 三者恰恰在新鲜度、成本、复杂度上系统性不同,工具名不同只是表象。
说反了:请求时最新鲜也最贵,批处理最不新鲜但最便宜。
对;新鲜度与成本同向递增,请求时逐请求算所以单点吞吐最低,这条单调链是选型基础。
流处理不是万能:它成本/复杂度高于批,新鲜度低于请求时,没有严格支配。
optionExplanations_en: They differ systematically on freshness, cost, and complexity; differing tool names are just surface.
Backwards: request-time is the freshest and priciest, while batch is the least fresh but cheapest.
Correct — freshness and cost rise together, and request-time computes per request so its throughput is lowest; this monotonic chain drives selection.
Streaming isn't universal: it costs and complicates more than batch and is less fresh than request-time, so it doesn't dominate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单位时间能处理多少记录;批/流可批量高吞吐,请求时逐条算所以低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Throughput is records processed per unit time; batch/streaming go high in bulk while request-time computes one at a time.

scenario: 要让「最近 5 分钟的点击计数」这种特征在线上随时可查,且延迟低。
scenario_en: You need a feature like 'clicks in the last 5 minutes' to be queryable online at any time with low latency.
q: 流处理管线的标准数据流是怎样的,特征最终落到哪里？
q_en: What is the standard streaming pipeline data flow, and where do features land?
why: 标准路径:事件进 Kafka → 流处理器(Flink/Kafka Streams)持续消费并物化特征 → 写入低延迟存储(Redis/DynamoDB)供在线查询。把「持续计算」和「快速读取」解耦,服务端只做一次 KV 查。
why_en: Events flow into Kafka, a stream processor continuously materializes features, and results land in a low-latency store like Redis/DynamoDB so serving only does a fast key lookup.
diagram:
flowchart LR E["事件"] --> K["Kafka
不可变日志"] K --> P["流处理器
Flink/Kafka Streams"] P --> D["低延迟存储
Redis/DynamoDB"] D --> Q["在线服务读取"]
options: 事件 → Kafka → 流处理器持续物化特征 → 写 Redis/DynamoDB → 在线服务读
事件 → 关系数据库 → 每晚跑一次报表 → 邮件发给分析师
事件 → 直接写模型权重 → 模型参数随每条事件实时更新
事件 → 对象存储归档 → 需要时手动下载解析
options_en: Events → Kafka → stream processor continuously materializes features → write Redis/DynamoDB → online serving reads.
Events → relational database → a nightly report job → email to analysts.
Events → written directly into model weights → parameters update per event in real time.
Events → object-storage archive → manually downloaded and parsed when needed.
optionExplanations: 对;Kafka 做事件总线、流处理器持续物化、KV 存储供低延迟读,是流特征管线的标准三段。
每晚报表是批处理离线分析,不能给在线服务低延迟查最近 5 分钟点击。
把事件塞进权重是在线学习的另一个话题,不是特征物化,也不是这里要的低延迟查询。
归档到对象存储是冷存,手动下载解析根本满足不了实时特征服务。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — Kafka as the event bus, a processor that continuously materializes, and a KV store for low-latency reads are the three standard segments.
A nightly report is offline batch analysis and can't serve last-5-minute clicks to online requests at low latency.
Feeding events into weights is online learning, a different topic, not feature materialization or the low-latency lookup needed here.
Archiving to object storage is cold storage; manual download can't serve real-time features.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式事件日志,不可变追加,充当流管线的事件总线与重放源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Kafka is a distributed, append-only event log that acts as the event bus and replay source for streaming pipelines.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把持续计算的结果预先写入存储,供在线查询,而非查询时才算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Materializing a feature means precomputing and writing its value to a store for online lookup rather than computing at query time.

scenario: 反欺诈要算「每张卡在滑动 10 分钟窗口内的交易次数」,跨数百万个卡号维护运行状态,还要 exactly-once 保证。
scenario_en: Fraud needs 'transaction count per card in a sliding 10-minute window', keeping running state across millions of card keys with exactly-once guarantees.
q: 这种大规模有状态窗口聚合,该选哪个流处理器？
q_en: For this large-scale stateful windowed aggregation, which stream processor fits?
why: Flink 是独立分布式引擎,原生支持事件时间窗口、跨海量 key 的有状态计算和 exactly-once,正好扛滑动窗口反欺诈。Kafka Streams 是嵌在应用 JVM 里的轻库,适合简单富化/计数,扛不动这种规模的状态。
why_en: Flink is a distributed engine with native event-time windowing, large-scale stateful compute, and exactly-once, fitting sliding-window fraud, while Kafka Streams is a lightweight in-JVM library for simpler enrichment.
tradeoff: Flink(独立集群、重状态、exactly-once) vs Kafka Streams(嵌 JVM、轻量、无独立集群)

rows: 大规模有状态+事件时间窗口

options: Kafka Streams:嵌在应用 JVM 里最省事,直接扛数百万 key 的滑动窗口状态
Apache Flink:独立分布式引擎,原生事件时间窗口 + 大规模有状态 + exactly-once,正合滑动窗口反欺诈
两个都不行,滑动窗口只能用批处理每小时重算一次
随便选,Flink 和 Kafka Streams 在状态规模和部署上没有区别
options_en: Kafka Streams: embedding in the app JVM is simplest and directly carries millions of keys of sliding-window state.
Apache Flink: a distributed engine with native event-time windowing, large-scale stateful compute, and exactly-once, fitting sliding-window fraud.
Neither works; sliding windows can only be recomputed hourly by batch.
Either is fine — Flink and Kafka Streams don't differ in state scale or deployment.
whenOtherWins: 若只是给事件做简单富化或轻量计数、且不想运维独立集群,嵌入应用 JVM 的 Kafka Streams 反而更合适。
whenOtherWins_en: If you only need simple event enrichment or lightweight counts and want no separate cluster to operate, in-JVM Kafka Streams is the better fit.
optionExplanations: Kafka Streams 轻量、本地状态,扛不住跨数百万 key 的大规模有状态窗口,规模一上来就吃力。
对;Flink 的事件时间窗口 + 大规模状态 + exactly-once 恰好命中滑动窗口反欺诈的三个硬需求。
批处理小时级重算满足不了反欺诈的分钟级窗口,把实时需求硬塞回批处理是退步。
两者在部署(独立集群 vs 嵌 JVM)和状态规模上差别很大,不能随便选。
optionExplanations_en: Kafka Streams is lightweight with local state and can't carry large-scale stateful windows across millions of keys once scale grows.
Correct — Flink's event-time windowing, large-scale state, and exactly-once hit the three hard needs of sliding-window fraud.
Hourly batch recompute can't meet fraud's minute-scale window; forcing a real-time need back into batch is a regression.
They differ sharply in deployment (separate cluster vs in-JVM) and state scale, so it's not an arbitrary pick.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Flink:独立分布式流引擎,支持事件时间窗口、大规模有状态计算和 exactly-once。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink (Apache Flink) is a distributed stream engine with event-time windowing, large-scale stateful compute, and exactly-once.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Kafka:分布式不可变事件日志,充当流管线的事件总线与重放源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka (Apache Kafka) is a distributed, immutable event log serving as the event bus and replay source for streaming pipelines.

termDefinitions.meaning: 嵌在应用 JVM 里的轻量流处理库,无需独立集群,适合简单富化/计数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka Streams is a lightweight stream-processing library embedded in the app JVM, needing no separate cluster, for simple enrichment/counts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每条事件对结果的影响恰好计入一次,不重不漏,保证聚合正确。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exactly-once means each event affects the result precisely once, neither dropped nor double-counted, keeping aggregates correct.

scenario: 用流处理维护「滚动 10 分钟平均值」,某个流处理器节点在半路崩溃了。
scenario_en: A streaming job maintains a rolling 10-minute average, and one processor node crashes midway.
q: 流处理最主要的复杂度来自哪里,崩溃后怎么不丢窗口结果？
q_en: Where does streaming's main complexity come from, and how do you avoid losing window results on crash?
why: 滚动窗口要记住此前事件,状态管理就是主要复杂度来源。链条:持续更新窗口态 → 定期 checkpoint 落盘 → 崩溃后从 checkpoint 恢复 + 从 Kafka 重放其后事件 → 续算;代价是迟到/乱序事件要专门处理。
why_en: The main complexity is state: a rolling window must remember prior events, so it checkpoints periodically and, on crash, restores from the last checkpoint and replays later Kafka events.
options: 复杂度来自选颜色主题;崩溃后直接重启进程就能自动恢复窗口结果,完全不需要 checkpoint 机制
复杂度来自 SQL 语法;崩溃后从最早的位点把全部历史事件从头重放一遍即可,不需要任何状态快照
复杂度来自状态管理:持续更新窗口态→定期 checkpoint→崩溃后从 checkpoint 恢复+Kafka 重放后续→续算,代价是处理迟到/乱序
流处理本质无状态,窗口结果只存在内存里,任何节点崩溃都会永久丢失且没有任何恢复手段
options_en: Complexity is picking a color theme; on crash just restart the process to auto-recover window results, needing no checkpoint mechanism at all.
Complexity is SQL syntax; on crash replay all history from the earliest offset from scratch, needing no state snapshot whatsoever.
Complexity is state management: continuously update window state → periodic checkpoint → on crash restore + replay later Kafka events → resume, at the cost of handling late/out-of-order.
Streaming is fundamentally stateless; window results live only in memory and any node crash loses them permanently with no recovery path.
optionExplanations: 颜色主题跟流处理无关;裸重启会丢内存里的窗口状态,正是要靠 checkpoint 才能恢复。
从头重放全部历史又慢又不必要;checkpoint 的意义就是只重放快照之后的事件。
对;走完「更新态→checkpoint→崩溃→恢复+重放→续算」整链;恢复靠快照加重放,业务还须容忍可能的重复处理。
流处理恰恰是有状态的;checkpoint + Kafka 重放正是为了让崩溃后能恢复窗口,不是无法恢复。
optionExplanations_en: Color theme is irrelevant; a bare restart loses in-memory window state, which is exactly why checkpoints exist.
Replaying all history is slow and unnecessary; checkpointing means you only replay events after the snapshot.
Correct — it walks the full chain update → checkpoint → crash → restore + replay → resume, at the cost of handling late/out-of-order events.
Streaming is stateful; checkpoints plus Kafka replay exist precisely so windows survive a crash, not the opposite.

termDefinitions.meaning: 定期把流处理的运行状态快照落盘,崩溃后可从最近一次恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint periodically snapshots the streaming job's state to durable storage so it can restore after a crash.

termDefinitions.term: late / out-of-order event / 迟到乱序事件
termDefinitions.meaning: 晚到或次序错乱的事件,窗口聚合必须优雅处理否则结果偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Late/out-of-order events arrive delayed or reordered and window aggregations must handle them gracefully or results skew.

termDefinitions.meaning: 维护窗口所需的历史事件与运行态,是流处理的主要复杂度来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: State management maintains the historical events and running state a window needs, the main source of streaming complexity.

scenario: 流管线出了 bug 算错了特征,或想给新特征回填历史,团队问「原始事件还在吗、怎么重来一遍」。
scenario_en: The streaming pipeline had a bug or you want to backfill a new feature; the team asks whether raw events still exist and how to recompute.
q: 为什么说 Kafka 的不可变追加日志是流管线的「真相源」？
q_en: Why is Kafka's immutable append-only log the source of truth for a streaming pipeline?
why: Kafka 只追加、不改写,原始事件按序完整保留。因此可以从任意位点重放事件来重算特征、回填历史、或在故障后恢复——重放同一份日志得到确定结果,相当于给流处理一个「可重来」的底座。
why_en: Kafka only appends and never rewrites, so raw events stay intact and ordered, letting you replay from any offset to recompute, backfill, or recover deterministically.
options: 因为它会自动纠正错误事件,重放时把之前写脏的数据改对再交给下游
因为日志只追加不改写,原始事件完整有序保留,可从任意位点重放来重算/回填/故障恢复
因为它把特征的最终值也一并存一份,在线服务端直接读这个成品值就行,不必重算
因为它会压缩掉历史事件只留每个键的最新状态,靠丢弃旧数据来节省存储成本
options_en: Because it auto-corrects bad events, cleaning previously dirty data on replay before handing off downstream.
Because the log is append-only and never rewritten, keeping raw events intact and ordered so you can replay from any offset to recompute/backfill/recover.
Because it also stores the final feature values, so online serving reads the finished value directly without recomputing.
Because it compacts away history keeping only each key's latest state, saving storage cost by discarding old data.
optionExplanations: Kafka 不会「纠正」事件,它忠实保留原样;重算的正确性来自可确定重放,不是自动改数据。
对;不可变追加保证原始事件可信可重放,这正是重算、回填、恢复的基础。
特征最终值落在下游 KV 存储,不是 Kafka 日志的职责;日志存的是原始事件。
默认日志按时间/大小保留原始事件供重放;compaction 是可选策略,不是「真相源」的理由。
optionExplanations_en: Kafka doesn't 'correct' events; it faithfully keeps them, and recompute correctness comes from deterministic replay, not auto-editing.
Correct — append-only immutability makes raw events trustworthy and replayable, the basis for recompute, backfill, and recovery.
Final feature values live in the downstream KV store, not the Kafka log, which holds raw events.
By default the log retains raw events by time/size for replay; compaction is optional and not the reason it's the source of truth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在末尾追加、从不修改历史条目的日志结构,天然可重放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An append-only log only appends at the end and never mutates past entries, making it naturally replayable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从日志的某个位点重新消费事件,以重算特征、回填或故障恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Event replay re-consumes events from an offset to recompute features, backfill, or recover from failure.

scenario: 结账页要用「用户当前购物车总额」当特征;这个值随点击秒变,且只在这次请求里有意义,单请求延迟预算个位数毫秒。
scenario_en: Checkout needs 'current cart total' as a feature; it changes per click, matters only for this request, and the per-request budget is single-digit ms.
q: 这种「当前请求上下文」特征最该用哪种范式算？
q_en: Which paradigm best computes this 'current request context' feature?
why: 购物车总额随点击秒变、且只在本次请求有意义,预物化没意义,应在预测请求里请求时同步现算。代价是它落在服务关键路径上、加延迟,所以只能做简单查表/加总,不能塞 10 分钟窗口那种重计算。
why_en: The cart total changes per click and only matters this request, so precomputing is pointless — compute it request-time inside the prediction call, at the cost of adding serving-path latency, so keep it to simple lookups.
tradeoff: 请求时(最新鲜但吃服务延迟预算,只能轻算) vs 预物化(不吃延迟但对秒变值无意义)
options: 每天批处理预算一次购物车总额,存 KV 供结账读
请求时同步现算:在预测请求里直接读购物车加总,最新鲜,代价是吃服务延迟只能轻算
用流处理为每个用户维护常驻购物车窗口,持续物化总额
训练时把购物车总额固化进模型权重,线上不再计算
options_en: Batch-precompute the cart total daily and store in a KV for checkout to read.
Compute it request-time: sum the cart directly inside the prediction call — freshest, at the cost of serving latency so keep it light.
Use streaming to keep a resident per-user cart window continuously materializing the total.
Bake the cart total into model weights at training time and never compute it online.
whenOtherWins: 若这个特征其实变化缓慢、可复用(如用户 30 天均消费),就该预物化到 KV,不该在每次请求现算白吃延迟。
whenOtherWins_en: If the feature actually changes slowly and is reusable (e.g. a user's 30-day average spend), precompute it to a KV instead of paying request-time latency each call.
optionExplanations: 日频批算购物车总额毫无意义:等下次跑批时用户早就结完账了,值也过期了。
对;秒变且只此一次的上下文特征就该请求时现算,轻量加总正好放进个位数毫秒预算。
为每个用户常驻购物车窗口是巨大浪费:购物车总额是本次请求现读的事,不值得维护常驻状态。
固化进权重是训练期常量,完全无法反映用户此刻的购物车,答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: Daily batch of the cart total is pointless: by the next run the user has checked out and the value is stale.
Correct — a per-click, single-use context feature should be computed request-time, and a light sum fits the single-digit-ms budget.
A resident cart window per user is huge waste: the cart total is read fresh this request and isn't worth maintaining as state.
Baking into weights is a training-time constant that can't reflect the user's cart right now, answering the wrong question.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在预测请求内同步现算特征,最新鲜但占用服务延迟预算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Request-time computation calculates a feature synchronously inside the prediction request, freshest but consuming the serving latency budget.

scenario: 有人提议在预测请求里请求时现算一个「用户最近 10 分钟行为的滑动窗口聚合」,单请求延迟预算只有个位数毫秒。
scenario_en: Someone proposes computing a user's rolling 10-minute behavioral window request-time inside the prediction call, with only a single-digit-ms budget.
q: 为什么请求时范式不适合算 10 分钟滑动窗口这种特征？
q_en: Why is request-time the wrong paradigm for a 10-minute sliding window?
why: 请求时计算直接加在服务关键路径上,吃掉本就紧张的个位数毫秒预算,所以只能做简单查表/算术。10 分钟窗口要拉历史事件、维护状态,根本塞不进这点预算——它属于流处理预物化的活。
why_en: Request-time compute sits on the serving critical path and eats the tight single-digit-ms budget, so it fits only simple lookups, not a 10-minute window that needs history and state.
options: 因为请求时在服务关键路径上、预算个位数毫秒,只够简单查表;10 分钟窗口要拉历史/维护状态,该交给流处理预物化
因为请求时算出来的特征天生不够新鲜,10 分钟窗口在这里反而比日频批处理还要陈旧,得不偿失
因为请求时的服务进程被禁止访问用户历史事件,权限层面就拿不到算 10 分钟窗口所需的数据
因为 10 分钟滑动窗口聚合必须在 GPU 上做,而请求时的服务节点只配了 CPU 跑不动它
options_en: Because request-time is on the serving critical path with a single-digit-ms budget fit only for simple lookups; a 10-minute window needs history/state and belongs to streaming precomputation.
Because request-time features are inherently not fresh enough, and a 10-minute window here ends up staler than daily batch, not worth it.
Because the request-time serving process is forbidden from accessing user history events, so permissions block getting the data the window needs.
Because a 10-minute sliding-window aggregation must run on a GPU, while request-time serving nodes only have CPUs and can't handle it.
optionExplanations: 对;关键路径 + 个位数毫秒预算只容得下轻量算术,重窗口聚合会顶破 p99,应由流处理提前物化。
说反了:请求时是最新鲜的范式,问题不在新鲜度,而在它吃服务延迟、只能轻算。
不是权限问题;请求时并非不能访问历史,而是在预算内来不及做重历史聚合。
GPU/CPU 不是这里的约束;瓶颈是延迟预算容不下窗口聚合的计算量。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the critical path plus a single-digit-ms budget allows only light arithmetic; a heavy window would blow p99 and should be pre-materialized by streaming.
Backwards: request-time is the freshest paradigm; the issue isn't freshness but that it eats serving latency and must stay light.
Not a permissions issue; request-time can access history but can't finish a heavy historical aggregation within budget.
GPU/CPU isn't the constraint here; the bottleneck is the latency budget not fitting the window's compute.

termDefinitions.term: serving critical path / 服务关键路径
termDefinitions.meaning: 从收到请求到返回预测的同步链路,任何计算都直接加进用户延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The serving critical path is the synchronous route from request to prediction, where any compute adds directly to user latency.

scenario: Airbnb 搜索一次请求里同时要:房源可订/价格、房东质量分、用户当前的搜索筛选条件三类特征。
scenario_en: One Airbnb search request needs three feature types: listing availability/price, host quality score, and the user's current search filters.
q: 把这三类特征分别配到最合适的范式,正确搭配是？
q_en: Matched to the best paradigm, what's the correct pairing for these three feature types?
why: 同一系统按每个特征的新鲜度需求混用范式:房源可订/价格分钟级变→流处理;房东质量分慢变→批处理;用户当前筛选条件本次请求才知道→请求时现算。多数真实系统都是这种混合体。
why_en: One system mixes paradigms per feature: availability/price change by the minute so streaming, host quality is slow so batch, and current search filters are known only now so request-time.
tradeoff: 按每个特征各自新鲜度需求分配范式(混合、各得其所) vs 全系统统一一种范式(简单但牺牲成本或新鲜度)
options: 三类特征全用批处理每晚统一算一次,简单一致
可订/价格→流处理;房东质量分→批处理;当前搜索筛选→请求时,各按新鲜度需求配范式
三类全用请求时现算,保证都最新鲜
可订/价格→批处理;房东质量分→请求时;当前搜索筛选→流处理
options_en: Compute all three with batch nightly for simplicity and consistency.
Availability/price → streaming; host quality → batch; current search filters → request-time, each matched to its freshness need.
Compute all three request-time to guarantee maximum freshness.
Availability/price → batch; host quality → request-time; current search filters → streaming.
whenOtherWins: 若某个平台的房源价格其实一天只调一次(长租、固定定价),那价格特征也可降到批处理,不必上流处理。
whenOtherWins_en: If a platform's listing prices actually change once a day (long-term stays, fixed pricing), the price feature can drop to batch rather than streaming.
optionExplanations: 全批处理会让分钟级变化的可订/价格和只此一次的搜索筛选都严重过期,牺牲了必要新鲜度。
对;按每个特征的新鲜度需求分别配范式,是真实系统的标准做法,也体现成本意识。
全请求时会把慢变的房东质量分也塞进服务路径白吃延迟,得不偿失。
搭配全错:价格该流、房东分该批、筛选该请求时,这个选项把三者对调了。
optionExplanations_en: All-batch leaves minute-scale availability/price and single-use search filters badly stale, sacrificing needed freshness.
Correct — matching each feature to its freshness need is standard practice in real systems and shows cost awareness.
All-request-time forces slow host-quality scores onto the serving path, wasting latency for no gain.
All wrong: price should stream, host score should batch, filters should be request-time — this option swaps them.

termDefinitions.term: hybrid feature pipeline / 混合特征管线
termDefinitions.meaning: 同一系统按每个特征的新鲜度需求混用批/流/请求时三种范式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hybrid feature pipeline mixes batch/streaming/request-time paradigms within one system per each feature's freshness need.

scenario: 团队要把「历史精确重算」和「近实时更新」两种需求合到一套特征架构里,在 Lambda 与 Kappa 之间选。
scenario_en: The team must serve both exact historical recompute and near-real-time updates in one feature architecture, choosing between Lambda and Kappa.
q: Lambda 与 Kappa 架构的核心区别在哪条轴上？
q_en: On what axis do Lambda and Kappa architectures fundamentally differ?
why: 核心区别是「几条代码路径」:Lambda 并行跑批层(求正确)和速度层(求低延迟)两套代码;Kappa 去掉批层,只用一条流管线,靠 Kafka 事件重放兼顾历史与实时。
why_en: The core difference is codepaths: Lambda runs parallel batch and speed layers, while Kappa drops the batch layer and uses a single stream pipeline with event replay for both history and real-time.
tradeoff: Lambda(双代码路径:批+流并行,易漂移) vs Kappa(单代码路径:纯流+重放,需成熟流基建)

rows: 双路径漂移→训练服务偏斜

options: 区别在编程语言:Lambda 用 Python、Kappa 用 Java,逻辑其实一样
区别在代码路径数:Lambda 批层+速度层两套并行;Kappa 只一条流管线,靠事件重放兼顾历史与实时
区别在存储引擎:Lambda 用 SQL、Kappa 用 NoSQL,和批流无关
区别在模型类型:Lambda 只能配线性模型、Kappa 只能配深度模型
options_en: The difference is language: Lambda uses Python and Kappa uses Java; the logic is the same.
The difference is codepath count: Lambda runs parallel batch and speed layers; Kappa uses a single stream pipeline with event replay for both history and real-time.
The difference is storage engine: Lambda uses SQL and Kappa uses NoSQL, unrelated to batch/stream.
The difference is model type: Lambda only fits linear models and Kappa only fits deep models.
optionExplanations: 语言不是分界;两者的真正差异是有几条并行代码路径处理同一份数据。
对;Lambda 双路径(批+速度)、Kappa 单路径(纯流+重放),这决定了漂移风险与基建要求。
存储引擎不是 Lambda/Kappa 的定义轴;它们讲的是批+流并行还是纯流单路径。
两种架构都与具体模型类型无关,不存在只能配某类模型的限制。
optionExplanations_en: Language isn't the divide; the real difference is how many parallel codepaths process the same data.
Correct — Lambda is dual-path (batch + speed), Kappa is single-path (pure stream + replay), which sets drift risk and infra needs.
Storage engine isn't the defining axis; the distinction is batch+stream parallel vs pure-stream single path.
Neither architecture is tied to a model type; there's no restriction to a particular model class.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并行跑批层(全量正确)与速度层(近实时低延迟),服务层合并两者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lambda architecture runs a batch layer for correctness and a speed layer for low latency in parallel, merged at serving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 去掉批层,只用一条流管线,靠事件重放同时做实时与历史重算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kappa architecture drops the batch layer and uses a single stream pipeline, doing real-time and historical recompute via event replay.

scenario: Lambda 架构里同一套特征逻辑要在 Spark(批层)和 Flink(速度层)里各实现一遍。
scenario_en: In Lambda, the same feature logic is implemented once in Spark (batch layer) and once in Flink (speed layer).
q: Lambda 的「双代码路径」最主要会引发什么问题？
q_en: What's the main problem caused by Lambda's dual codepath?
why: 同一逻辑写两遍(Spark + Flink),两边随时间实现漂移 → 训练用一套、服务用另一套时特征算得不一样 → 训练-服务偏斜,模型线上掉点;而且开发/维护工作量翻倍。这正是 Kappa 想用单路径消除的痛点。
why_en: Implementing the same logic twice drifts over time, so training and serving compute features differently — training-serving skew — plus doubled dev effort, which Kappa's single path aims to remove.
options: 会让特征算得更准,因为两套实现可以互相校验纠错
两套实现随时间漂移→训练与服务特征不一致→训练-服务偏斜+开发维护翻倍
只会增加一点存储,对模型质量没有任何影响
会自动触发模型重训,反而让模型一直保持最新
options_en: It makes features more accurate because the two implementations cross-check and correct each other.
The two implementations drift over time → training and serving features diverge → training-serving skew plus doubled dev/maintenance.
It only adds a little storage with no effect on model quality.
It auto-triggers retraining, keeping the model always up to date.
optionExplanations: 两套实现不会互相纠错,反而各自演化;没有单一真相,漂移只会更难发现。
对;逻辑写两遍必然漂移,导致训练-服务偏斜和双倍工作量,这是 Lambda 的招牌代价。
问题不在存储,而在两条路径算出不一样的特征,直接伤模型线上表现。
双路径不会自动重训;它带来的是特征不一致的隐患,不是自动更新的好处。
optionExplanations_en: The two implementations don't correct each other; they evolve separately, and with no single truth drift is harder to catch.
Correct — writing logic twice inevitably drifts, causing training-serving skew and double the work, Lambda's signature cost.
The problem isn't storage but two paths computing different features, directly hurting online model performance.
Dual paths don't auto-retrain; they create a feature-inconsistency hazard, not an auto-update benefit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一特征逻辑在批与流各实现一遍,易随时间漂移不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dual-codepath means the same feature logic is implemented in both batch and stream, prone to drifting apart over time.

scenario: 一家大厂有成熟的 Kafka + Flink 流基建,能扛大规模事件重放与 checkpoint 恢复,想减少特征逻辑重复实现带来的偏斜。
scenario_en: A big-tech team has mature Kafka+Flink infra able to handle large-scale replay and checkpoint recovery, and wants to reduce skew from duplicated feature logic.
q: 这种情况下 Lambda 与 Kappa 更该选谁？
q_en: Given this, should they lean Lambda or Kappa?
why: 有成熟流基建又想消除双路径偏斜时,Kappa 更合适:单条流管线 + Kafka 重放同时做实时和历史,逻辑只写一遍,漂移和维护量都降。前提正是它对流基建成熟度要求高。
why_en: With mature streaming infra and a goal of killing dual-path skew, Kappa fits: one stream pipeline plus replay handles real-time and history with logic written once.
tradeoff: Kappa(单路径省偏斜,但要成熟流基建) vs Lambda(批流逻辑天生不同或有遗留约束时更现实)
options: Lambda,因为无论何时双路径都比单路径可靠
无所谓,两者在偏斜和维护量上没差别
Kappa:成熟流基建下单管线+重放消除双路径偏斜,逻辑只写一遍
都不选,应退回纯批处理放弃实时需求
options_en: Lambda, because dual paths are always more reliable than a single path.
It doesn't matter; the two are identical on skew and maintenance.
Kappa: with mature infra a single pipeline plus replay removes dual-path skew and logic is written once.
Neither; fall back to pure batch and drop the real-time need.
whenOtherWins: 若批处理与流处理的业务逻辑本质不同,或有遗留系统挡住 Kappa 迁移,Lambda 仍然更现实。
whenOtherWins_en: If batch and streaming logic genuinely differ, or legacy systems block a Kappa migration, Lambda remains the more realistic choice.
optionExplanations: 双路径不是「更可靠」,它恰恰引入漂移;Lambda 的优势另有前提(逻辑天生不同/遗留约束)。
两者差别很大:Kappa 单路径省偏斜但要成熟基建,Lambda 双路径反之,不能说没差别。
对;既有成熟流基建又想去偏斜,Kappa 的单路径正好命中,逻辑一处维护。
退回纯批会丢掉近实时需求,不是这道题要的权衡,属于因噎废食。
optionExplanations_en: Dual paths aren't 'more reliable'; they introduce drift, and Lambda's edge has other conditions (genuinely different logic/legacy).
They differ a lot: Kappa's single path cuts skew but needs mature infra, Lambda is the reverse, so not identical.
Correct — with mature streaming infra and a skew-reduction goal, Kappa's single path hits the mark with one place to maintain logic.
Falling back to pure batch drops the near-real-time need, not the tradeoff asked, and throws out the baby with the bathwater.

termDefinitions.term: streaming infra maturity / 流基建成熟度
termDefinitions.meaning: 能稳定支撑大规模事件重放、状态管理、checkpoint 恢复与 exactly-once 的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Streaming infra maturity is the ability to reliably support large-scale replay, state management, checkpoint recovery, and exactly-once.

scenario: 反欺诈系统需要一个特征:某张卡在最近 10 分钟内的交易次数,用来实时拦截盗刷。
scenario_en: A fraud system needs a feature: a card's transaction count in the last 10 minutes, to block theft in real time.
q: 算「最近 10 分钟卡交易次数」该用哪种管线？
q_en: Which pipeline computes 'card transactions in the last 10 minutes'?
why: 这是分钟级新鲜、需跨事件维护滑动窗口计数的典型信号,正是流处理的有状态窗口聚合。批处理太旧、请求时又扛不住在预算内做窗口聚合,只有流处理能持续物化这个计数。
why_en: This is a minute-fresh, cross-event sliding-window count — exactly streaming's stateful windowed aggregation — since batch is too stale and request-time can't do the window within budget.
tradeoff: 流处理(有状态窗口、分钟级新鲜) vs 批(太旧) / 请求时(预算内做不了窗口)
options: 批处理每日聚合,凌晨统一算一次卡交易数
请求时在拦截请求里现场扫这张卡 10 分钟的全部交易
静态规则:每张卡固定阈值,不看时间窗口
流处理的有状态窗口聚合:持续维护每张卡的滑动 10 分钟计数
options_en: Batch daily aggregation, computing the card's transaction count once overnight.
Request-time: scan all of this card's 10-minute transactions live inside the blocking request.
A static rule: a fixed threshold per card, ignoring the time window.
Streaming stateful windowed aggregation: continuously maintain a sliding 10-minute count per card.
whenOtherWins: 若欺诈判断只需「该卡历史累计交易数」这种慢变量,不要求分钟级窗口,那批处理反而更省。
whenOtherWins_en: If the fraud check only needs a slow signal like the card's lifetime transaction count, not a minute-scale window, batch is cheaper.
optionExplanations: 日频批的计数最坏差近 24 小时,盗刷早就完成了,分钟级拦截靠不住它。
在拦截请求里现扫 10 分钟全量交易会吃爆延迟预算,窗口聚合不该放服务关键路径。
静态阈值不看时间分布,抓不住「短时间内异常高频」这一欺诈信号的关键。
对;分钟级新鲜 + 跨事件滑动窗口正是流处理有状态聚合的主场,持续物化该计数供实时拦截。
optionExplanations_en: A daily count can be nearly 24h off; the theft is long done, so minute-scale blocking can't rely on it.
Live-scanning 10 minutes of transactions in the blocking request blows the latency budget; window aggregation shouldn't sit on the critical path.
A static threshold ignores timing and misses the key fraud signal of abnormally high frequency in a short span.
Correct — minute freshness plus a cross-event sliding window is streaming's stateful-aggregation home turf, materializing the count for real-time blocking.

termDefinitions.term: sliding window aggregation / 滑动窗口聚合
termDefinitions.meaning: 对不断推进的时间窗口内事件做聚合(如计数),需跨事件维护状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sliding-window aggregation computes over events in a continuously advancing time window, requiring cross-event state.

q: 把「按新鲜度选特征管线」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the decision chain for choosing a feature pipeline by freshness:
steps: 分钟级容忍(滚动欺诈、会话参与、趋势分)→ 流处理
先问:这个特征必须多新鲜？
小时级容忍(人口属性、30 天聚合、预训练 embedding)→ 批处理(最便宜)
请求范围内才有意义(购物车、当前 query、设备上下文)→ 请求时
why: 选型永远从「多新鲜」这个问题起手,再沿新鲜度递增分档:小时级→批(最便宜)、分钟级→流、只此请求→请求时。新鲜度定档后,成本和复杂度随之而定。
why_en: Selection always starts from 'how fresh?', then tiers by rising freshness: hours to batch, minutes to streaming, this-request-only to request-time, with cost following.
diagram:
flowchart TD Q["这个特征必须多新鲜?"] --> H["小时级容忍
→ 批处理(最便宜)"] Q --> M["分钟级容忍
→ 流处理"] Q --> R["仅本请求有意义
→ 请求时"]

termDefinitions.term: freshness-first selection / 新鲜度优先选型
termDefinitions.meaning: 先确定特征所需新鲜度,再据此选批/流/请求时,成本随新鲜度上升。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Freshness-first selection fixes the required freshness, then picks batch/streaming/request-time, with cost rising with freshness.

q: 填空:三档新鲜度需求各自对应的管线。
q_en: Fill in the pipeline matching each freshness tier.
text: 小时级容忍(30 天聚合、预训练 embedding)→ {{批处理}};分钟级容忍(滚动欺诈、会话参与)→ {{流处理}};仅当前请求有意义(购物车、当前 query)→ {{请求时}}。
text_en: Hours-tolerant (30-day aggregates, pretrained embeddings) → {{batch}}; minutes-tolerant (rolling fraud, session engagement) → {{streaming}}; only this-request meaningful (cart, current query) → {{request-time}}.
why: 记住这条映射就能秒答选型题:档位由新鲜度决定,成本沿批→流→请求时递增。面试里按「特征名 + 新鲜度 + 成本」一句话给出理由即可。
why_en: Memorize this mapping to answer selection fast: the tier follows freshness and cost rises batch to streaming to request-time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把特征按可容忍陈旧度分成小时/分钟/请求三档,一档对应一种管线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A freshness tier buckets features by tolerable staleness into hours/minutes/request, each mapping to one pipeline.

scenario: 面试官问「这三种范式的成本差在哪」,想听你说清成本是怎么随新鲜度叠上去的。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks where the cost difference lies across the three paradigms and how cost layers onto freshness.
q: 成本是如何在批/流/请求时之间叠加的？
q_en: How does cost layer across batch, streaming, and request-time?
why: 成本沿新鲜度叠加:批处理每条记录最便宜(可用 spot、按需跑完即停);流处理是 always-on 常驻 + 状态管理开销;请求时不额外买机器,但吃掉服务延迟预算(等于占用最贵的在线资源)。三者成本形态不同,不能只比机器价。
why_en: Cost layers onto freshness: batch is cheapest per record (spot, run-and-stop), streaming pays always-on plus state overhead, and request-time consumes the serving latency budget itself.
options: 三种范式的单位成本完全一样,选谁都不影响账单,只是不同运维团队的使用习惯不同罢了
请求时是最便宜的范式,因为它既不预先物化特征、也不额外占用任何存储空间,近乎零成本
批处理每条最便宜(spot、跑完即停);流处理 always-on+状态开销;请求时吃服务延迟预算
流处理是最便宜的范式,因为它不像批处理那样需要长期保存海量历史数据来支撑重算
options_en: All three have identical per-record cost; the choice doesn't affect the bill — it's just different ops-team habits.
Request-time is the cheapest paradigm because it neither pre-materializes features nor uses any extra storage, near zero cost.
Batch is cheapest per record (spot, run-and-stop); streaming pays always-on plus state overhead; request-time eats the serving latency budget.
Streaming is the cheapest paradigm because, unlike batch, it doesn't retain massive history long-term to support recompute.
optionExplanations: 成本形态明显不同:批可用 spot、流要常驻、请求时占在线预算,账单差别很大。
请求时不占额外机器不代表便宜——它消耗最贵的服务延迟预算,反而是最高成本范式。
对;成本沿新鲜度递增,批最便宜、请求时最贵、流居中,三者的成本来源各不相同。
流要常驻运行还要维护窗口状态,并不比批省;批用 spot 跑完即停才是成本最低的。
optionExplanations_en: The cost shapes clearly differ: batch can use spot, streaming stays resident, request-time takes online budget, so bills vary widely.
Not buying extra machines doesn't make request-time cheap — it consumes the priciest serving budget and is the costliest paradigm.
Correct — cost rises with freshness: batch cheapest, request-time priciest, streaming in between, each with a different cost source.
Streaming stays always-on and maintains state, not cheaper than batch; batch on spot that stops when done is the thriftiest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理需持续运行的集群与状态存储开销,即使流量低也要付。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Always-on cost is the continuously running cluster and state storage a stream needs, paid even at low traffic.

scenario: 面试里有人张口就说「所有特征都实时算」,或另一个人说「全批处理就行」,面试官在观察你的成本/延迟意识。
scenario_en: In an interview someone says 'compute every feature in real time', another says 'just batch everything', while the interviewer gauges your cost/latency awareness.
q: 「全实时」和「全批处理」这两种极端各暴露了什么弱点？
q_en: What weakness does each extreme — 'all real-time' and 'all batch' — reveal?
why: 「全部实时」暴露弱成本意识——为不需要新鲜的特征白付 always-on/延迟代价;「全部批处理」则漏掉了延迟敏感需求(反欺诈、会话)。强答案按特征逐个匹配新鲜度,并说出「这里批就够,因为新鲜度要求宽松」这类成本自觉。
why_en: 'All real-time' shows weak cost awareness (paying freshness cost where none is needed), while 'all batch' misses latency-sensitive needs; strong answers match freshness per feature.
options: 全实时暴露弱成本意识(为不需新鲜的特征白付代价);全批处理漏掉延迟敏感需求(反欺诈/会话)
两种极端其实都很好,能大幅简化架构、减少要维护的管线种类,面试官通常都会为简洁加分
全实时是最省钱的方案;全批处理是最新鲜的方案,所以这两个极端其实各自都是全局最优解
两种说法没有本质区别,选错了也没关系,反正上线后都能通过 A/B 测试观察指标再回头修正
options_en: All real-time reveals weak cost awareness (paying for freshness nobody needs); all batch misses latency-sensitive needs (fraud/session).
Both extremes are actually great — they simplify architecture and cut the pipeline types to maintain, so interviewers reward the simplicity.
All real-time is the cheapest option; all batch is the freshest option, so these two extremes are each a global optimum.
There's no real difference; picking wrong is fine because A/B testing after launch will catch the metrics and let you fix it later.
optionExplanations: 对;两个极端各踩一个坑——全实时浪费成本、全批处理误了延迟,逐特征匹配新鲜度才是强答案。
极端简化会牺牲成本或延迟,面试官恰恰在看你会不会按需匹配,不会给极端加分。
说反了:实时最贵不是最省,批最便宜但最不新鲜,没有哪个极端普遍最优。
选错范式带来的成本/延迟问题 A/B 测不出来,选型该在设计阶段用新鲜度需求定。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — each extreme hits a pitfall: all real-time wastes cost, all batch misses latency; per-feature freshness matching is the strong answer.
Extreme simplification sacrifices cost or latency; the interviewer looks for need-based matching and won't reward extremes.
Backwards: real-time is priciest not cheapest, and batch is cheapest but least fresh; no extreme is universally optimal.
A/B testing won't surface the cost/latency of a wrong paradigm; selection belongs in design, driven by freshness need.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只为真正需要的新鲜度付费,不给宽松特征上昂贵实时管线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cost awareness means paying only for the freshness truly needed, not putting relaxed features on expensive real-time pipelines.

scenario: 真实系统里批、流、请求时特征混着用,面试官问「这些异构管线最后怎么统一喂给训练和推理」。
scenario_en: Real systems mix batch, streaming, and request-time features; the interviewer asks how these heterogeneous pipelines are unified for training and inference.
q: 多数系统是混合体,靠什么层把异构管线统一、防止训练-服务偏斜？
q_en: Most systems are hybrids — what layer unifies the heterogeneous pipelines and prevents training-serving skew?
why: 特征存储(feature store)提供统一接口,把批和流的特征一致地供给训练与在线推理,让两侧读到同一份定义与值,从而防止训练-服务偏斜。Lambda/Kappa 决定管线怎么汇聚,feature store 决定怎么统一对外服务。
why_en: A feature store gives one interface that serves batch and streaming features consistently to both training and inference, preventing training-serving skew.
options: 靠 CDN 边缘缓存把算好的特征分发到各地节点,用就近读取来保证多个服务读到一致的特征
靠特征存储(feature store)统一接口,一致地把批+流特征供给训练与推理,防训练-服务偏斜
靠给每个用到特征的模型各自单独复制一份特征计算代码,让大家用同样的逻辑来对齐特征
靠一个每天定时运行的人工核对流程,逐一比对训练侧与线上服务侧的特征值是否一致
options_en: A CDN edge cache that distributes computed features to regional nodes, using nearby reads to keep multiple services consistent.
A feature store: one interface serving batch+streaming features consistently to training and inference, preventing training-serving skew.
Copying the feature-computation code separately into each model that uses it, aligning everyone via the same logic.
A daily scheduled manual reconciliation that compares training-side and online-serving feature values one by one.
optionExplanations: CDN 是内容分发,不解决训练与服务读到同一份特征定义的一致性问题。
对;feature store 就是那层统一接口,让训练和推理共享同一份特征值,系统性防偏斜。
给每个模型复制特征代码正是制造漂移的来源,与统一防偏斜的目标相反。
人工每天核对既不可扩展也不可靠,防偏斜要靠共享的特征存储而非人肉对账。
optionExplanations_en: A CDN is content delivery and doesn't solve training and serving reading the same feature definition.
Correct — the feature store is that unifying interface, letting training and inference share the same feature values and systematically preventing skew.
Copying feature code per model is itself a drift source, the opposite of unified skew prevention.
Daily manual reconciliation is neither scalable nor reliable; skew prevention needs a shared feature store, not human checking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一存取特征的系统,一致地把批+流特征供给训练与在线推理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store is a system for storing and serving features consistently to both training and online inference.

scenario: 要算「用户本次会话的参与度」「某内容最近的趋势热度」这类信号,分钟级更新即可,不必毫秒,但一天一次太旧。
scenario_en: You need signals like current-session engagement and recent trending score — minute-scale updates suffice, milliseconds unneeded, but daily is too stale.
q: 这类「分钟级新鲜」的信号最该用哪种管线？
q_en: Which pipeline fits these minute-fresh signals?
why: 会话参与度、趋势热度是分钟级容忍的滚动信号:批处理一天一次太旧,请求时又不该在服务路径做重聚合,流处理持续物化正好卡在中间。代价是常驻集群与状态管理开销。
why_en: Session engagement and trending are minute-tolerant rolling signals: batch is too stale and request-time shouldn't do heavy aggregation on the serving path, so streaming's continuous materialization fits.
tradeoff: 流处理(分钟级、持续物化) vs 批(太旧) / 请求时(不宜在路径上重聚合)
options: 批处理:每天算一次会话参与度和趋势热度
请求时:在每次预测里现算最近趋势热度的聚合
流处理:持续物化分钟级滚动信号,代价是常驻集群+状态开销
静态配置:给每个内容写死一个固定热度分
options_en: Batch: compute session engagement and trending once a day.
Request-time: compute the recent trending aggregate live in each prediction.
Streaming: continuously materialize minute-scale rolling signals, at the cost of a resident cluster plus state overhead.
Static config: hardcode a fixed trending score per content item.
whenOtherWins: 若「趋势热度」其实按天更新就够(如日榜),那降到批处理更省,不必上流处理常驻成本。
whenOtherWins_en: If trending only needs daily updates (a daily chart), drop to batch to save the streaming always-on cost.
optionExplanations: 日频批对分钟级容忍的会话/趋势信号太旧,会话结束了参与度还没更新。
在服务路径现算趋势聚合会吃延迟预算,分钟级信号不该占用请求时的轻算额度。
对;分钟级容忍 + 滚动聚合正是流处理的位置,持续物化供在线读,代价是常驻与状态。
写死热度分无法反映实时趋势,趋势信号的意义就在于它会随时间变化。
optionExplanations_en: Daily batch is too stale for minute-tolerant session/trending signals; the session ends before engagement updates.
Computing the trending aggregate on the serving path eats budget; minute-scale signals shouldn't use request-time's light quota.
Correct — minute tolerance plus rolling aggregation is streaming's spot, materializing continuously for online reads at the cost of resident state.
A hardcoded score can't reflect live trends; a trending signal exists precisely because it changes over time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反映内容近期热度的滚动信号,分钟级更新,依赖近期事件聚合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trending score reflects recent content popularity as a rolling, minute-scale signal built from recent-event aggregation.

q: 填空:Lambda 架构的三层各自职责。
q_en: Fill in the roles of Lambda architecture's three layers.
text: Lambda 的 {{批处理层}}(batch layer)对全量历史重算保证正确性,{{速度层}}(speed layer)处理近期事件保证低延迟,{{服务层}}(serving layer)合并两者对外提供查询。
text_en: Lambda's {{batch layer}} recomputes over full history for correctness, the {{speed layer}} handles recent events for low latency, and the {{serving layer}} merges both to answer queries.
why: 三层分工:批层求「对」、速度层求「快」、服务层做「合」。正因逻辑在批层与速度层各写一遍,才有 Lambda 招牌的双路径漂移风险。
why_en: Batch layer for correctness, speed layer for latency, serving layer to merge — and duplicating logic across batch and speed is where Lambda's drift risk comes from.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lambda 中合并批层与速度层结果、对外统一提供查询的层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The serving layer in Lambda merges batch and speed layer outputs to answer queries uniformly.

scenario: 对比批处理与请求时实时在「单位时间能处理多少记录」上的差别。
scenario_en: Contrasting batch and request-time on how many records each processes per unit time.
q: 在吞吐这条轴上,批处理和请求时为什么差这么多？
q_en: On the throughput axis, why do batch and request-time differ so much?
why: 批处理把上亿条记录打包成大 job 一次算完,吞吐极高;请求时是每来一个请求现算一条,天生逐条、吞吐低。差别根源是「批量 vs 逐请求」的处理粒度,不是硬件快慢。
why_en: Batch processes 100M+ records in one bulk job for very high throughput, while request-time computes one record per incoming request, so throughput is low by design.
tradeoff: 批处理(批量、高吞吐、不新鲜) vs 请求时(逐请求、低吞吐、最新鲜)
options: 批处理是逐条一个个算所以吞吐低,请求时反而是打包成批一次算完所以吞吐更高,和延迟无关
批处理批量整批算所以吞吐高,请求时逐请求现算一条所以吞吐低,根源是处理粒度
两者的吞吐其实完全一样,差别只在延迟:批处理慢一点、请求时快一点,吞吐维度上没有区分
请求时吞吐更高,因为它不用像批处理那样等待调度器排期,来一个请求立刻就能算出结果
options_en: Batch computes one by one so throughput is low, while request-time bundles into bulk so its throughput is higher — unrelated to latency.
Batch processes whole bulk sets for high throughput, request-time computes one record per request for low throughput — the root is processing granularity.
Their throughput is actually identical; the only difference is latency, batch a bit slower and request-time a bit faster, with no throughput gap.
Request-time has higher throughput because it never waits for a scheduler like batch does and computes the moment a request arrives.
optionExplanations: 说反了:批处理是批量算所以吞吐高,请求时才是逐条现算。
对;差别在粒度——批量 vs 逐请求,而非硬件;批适合百万-十亿/次,请求时是每请求一条。
吞吐并不一样:批量处理天然远高于逐请求现算,这正是两者的关键区分维度。
请求时逐条现算吞吐低;调度延迟不是这里的决定因素,粒度才是。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: batch computes in bulk for high throughput; request-time is the one computing per record.
Correct — the difference is granularity (bulk vs per request), not hardware; batch suits millions-billions per run, request-time one per request.
Throughput isn't the same: bulk processing is far higher than per-request compute, the key distinguishing dimension.
Request-time's per-record compute is low throughput; scheduling latency isn't the deciding factor, granularity is.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次处理的记录规模:批处理成批、请求时逐条,决定吞吐高低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Processing granularity is how many records are handled at once — bulk for batch, one-by-one for request-time — driving throughput.

q: 把流处理节点崩溃后的状态恢复流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the state-recovery flow after a streaming node crashes:
steps: 从最近一次 checkpoint 恢复窗口状态
处理器持续更新窗口状态并定期 checkpoint 落盘
从 Kafka 中重放 checkpoint 之后的事件补齐
某个流处理器节点崩溃,内存中窗口状态丢失
why: 恢复靠「快照 + 重放」两件套:平时定期 checkpoint,崩溃后先从最近 checkpoint 恢复状态,再从 Kafka 重放其后事件补齐,窗口即可续算。代价是恢复期短暂延迟,且业务要能容忍可能的重复处理。
why_en: Recovery uses snapshot plus replay: checkpoint regularly, then on crash restore from the last checkpoint and replay later Kafka events to catch up.
diagram:
flowchart LR U["持续更新+定期checkpoint"] --> C["节点崩溃
内存态丢失"] C --> R["从checkpoint恢复"] R --> P["Kafka重放后续事件"] P --> D["窗口续算"]

termDefinitions.term: checkpoint + replay recovery / 快照加重放恢复
termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理靠定期状态快照与 Kafka 事件重放,在崩溃后恢复窗口计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Checkpoint-plus-replay recovery uses periodic state snapshots and Kafka event replay to restore window computation after a crash.

scenario: 给信用评分模型算特征:征信聚合、历史还款行为。这些信号按天甚至更慢变化,监管也倾向可复现、可审计。
scenario_en: Features for a credit-scoring model: bureau aggregates and repayment history — signals that change daily or slower, with regulators favoring reproducibility and auditability.
q: 信用评分这类慢变、需可审计的特征,最该用哪种管线？
q_en: For slow-changing, auditable credit-scoring features, which pipeline fits best?
why: 征信/还款信号慢变,日频足够新鲜;批处理不仅最便宜,其有界输入 + 确定性输出天然可重放、可审计,正合监管要求。用流/请求时是白付实时成本还增加不可复现风险。
why_en: Bureau/repayment signals change slowly so daily is fresh enough, and batch's bounded, deterministic output is naturally reproducible and auditable, fitting regulation.
tradeoff: 批处理(慢变够新鲜、可重放可审计、最便宜) vs 流/请求时(白付实时成本、复现更难)
options: 请求时:在每次评分请求里现算征信聚合,追求毫秒新鲜
流处理:为每个用户维护常驻还款行为窗口,持续物化
静态规则:不用历史数据,直接按年龄段给固定分
批处理:日频算征信/还款聚合,有界确定性输出天然可重放可审计,也最便宜
options_en: Request-time: compute bureau aggregates live in each scoring request for millisecond freshness.
Streaming: keep a resident repayment-behavior window per user, materializing continuously.
Static rule: skip history and assign a fixed score by age bracket.
Batch: daily bureau/repayment aggregates whose bounded, deterministic output is naturally reproducible and auditable, and cheapest.
whenOtherWins: 若要在申请流程中实时纳入「刚刚发生的交易」这类分钟级信号,那部分特征才需要升级到流处理。
whenOtherWins_en: If the application flow must incorporate just-happened transactions in real time, those minute-scale features warrant streaming.
optionExplanations: 征信慢变,毫秒新鲜毫无必要;在评分请求里现算重聚合还会吃延迟、增加复现难度。
为慢变还款信号维护常驻流是浪费:always-on 成本白付,新鲜度也用不上。
抛开历史用固定分既不准也不合规,信用评分的信号价值就在历史行为里。
对;慢变 + 可审计正是批处理主场,确定性输出可重放、成本最低,契合监管。
optionExplanations_en: Bureau signals change slowly so millisecond freshness is pointless, and live heavy aggregation in the request eats latency and hurts reproducibility.
A resident stream for slow repayment signals is waste: always-on cost paid for freshness never used.
Dropping history for a fixed score is inaccurate and non-compliant; credit signal value lives in historical behavior.
Correct — slow-changing plus auditable is batch's home turf: deterministic output is replayable at the lowest cost, fitting regulation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能复现某次评分用的特征与结果;批处理确定性输出天然满足。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Auditability is being able to reproduce the features and result of a given score, which batch's deterministic output naturally supports.

scenario: 一个 Spark 批 job 要在上亿(100M+)条记录上算 30 天购买次数、平均会话时长、用户 embedding。
scenario_en: One Spark batch job computes 30-day purchase counts, average session durations, and user embeddings over 100M+ records.
q: 「一个 Spark job 覆盖 100M+ 记录」这个规模说明批处理的什么特点？
q_en: What does 'one Spark job over 100M+ records' say about batch's profile?
why: 100M+ 是数据规模量级(不是延迟目标):它说明批处理靠批量并行拿到极高吞吐,把海量历史一次算完,单位记录成本被摊到最低。代价是这份结果只到跑批时刻,不解决新鲜度。
why_en: The 100M+ is a data-scale magnitude showing batch's very high throughput via bulk parallelism, amortizing per-record cost, though results are only as fresh as the run.
options: 说明批处理靠批量并行拿到极高吞吐,单位记录成本最低,代价是结果只到跑批时刻
说明批处理延迟极低,能在毫秒内返回单条查询
说明批处理天然新鲜,100M 记录会实时更新
说明批处理必须用 GPU 才能处理这么多记录
options_en: It shows batch achieves very high throughput via bulk parallelism at the lowest per-record cost, at the cost of results only being run-fresh.
It shows batch has very low latency, returning a single query in milliseconds.
It shows batch is inherently fresh — the 100M records update in real time.
It shows batch must use GPUs to handle that many records.
optionExplanations: 对;100M+ 是吞吐/规模的证据,批量并行摊薄每条成本,但换来的是小时级陈旧。
批处理延迟高(小时级),不是毫秒查询;低延迟单查是请求时/流的低延迟存储的活。
批处理最不新鲜,100M 记录是一次跑批的输入,不会实时更新。
GPU 不是必需;这类聚合特征多在 CPU 集群上跑,规模靠并行而非 GPU。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — 100M+ is throughput/scale evidence: bulk parallelism amortizes per-record cost, but trades for hourly staleness.
Batch latency is high (hours), not millisecond queries; low-latency single lookups are the job of a request-time/stream low-latency store.
Batch is the least fresh; the 100M records are one run's input and don't update in real time.
GPUs aren't required; such aggregate features usually run on CPU clusters, scaling via parallelism not GPUs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把海量记录切分并行处理,一次 job 拿到高吞吐、低单位成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bulk parallelism splits massive records across workers so one job yields high throughput and low per-record cost.

scenario: 团队想迁到 Kappa,用单条流管线靠 Kafka 大规模事件重放同时做实时和历史重算。
scenario_en: A team wants to move to Kappa, using one stream pipeline with large-scale Kafka replay for both real-time and historical recompute.
q: Kappa 单路径的好处不是白来的,它对基建提出什么硬要求？
q_en: Kappa's single-path benefit isn't free — what hard infra requirement does it impose?
why: Kappa 用事件重放取代批层,所以要求成熟的流基建能扛大规模重放:稳健的状态管理、checkpoint 恢复、exactly-once 语义。基建不够成熟时,重放历史会压垮系统,这也是 Lambda 在有遗留约束时仍被保留的原因。
why_en: Kappa replaces the batch layer with replay, so it demands mature streaming infra for large-scale replay: robust state management, checkpoint recovery, and exactly-once.
options: 只要一台小机器就能把全部历史事件重放一遍,对底层流基建的能力没有任何额外要求
要求成熟流基建扛大规模重放:稳健状态管理、checkpoint 恢复、exactly-once
要求团队全员都会写 SQL 查询,只要人会写查询,流基建本身成熟不成熟其实无所谓
要求把历史事件数据全部删掉、只保留最近一小时,靠丢弃历史来降低重放的压力
options_en: A single small machine can replay all history; it places no extra demand on the underlying streaming infra at all.
It requires mature streaming infra for large-scale replay: robust state management, checkpoint recovery, and exactly-once.
It requires the whole team to write SQL queries; as long as people can query, the infra's maturity doesn't matter.
It requires deleting all history events and keeping only the last hour, easing replay by discarding the past.
optionExplanations: 大规模历史重放要分布式流基建支撑,小机器扛不住,这正是 Kappa 的门槛。
对;单路径省了漂移,但把担子压给流基建,必须成熟到能大规模重放并保证 exactly-once。
会不会 SQL 不是关键;Kappa 的硬要求是流基建的重放与状态恢复能力。
Kappa 恰恰要靠保留历史事件来重放重算,删掉历史就做不了历史重算了。
optionExplanations_en: Large-scale historical replay needs distributed streaming infra; a small machine can't carry it, which is Kappa's bar.
Correct — the single path removes drift but shifts the load to streaming infra, which must be mature enough for large-scale replay with exactly-once.
SQL skills aren't the point; Kappa's hard requirement is the infra's replay and state-recovery capability.
Kappa relies on retaining historical events to replay and recompute; deleting history makes historical recompute impossible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从 Kafka 重新消费海量历史事件来重算,Kappa 用它替代批层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Large-scale replay re-consumes massive historical Kafka events to recompute, which Kappa uses in place of a batch layer.

scenario: 有候选人把流处理说成「就是更快的批处理」,准备无脑给所有近实时特征上流。
scenario_en: A candidate calls streaming 'just faster batch' and plans to put every near-real-time feature on it without thought.
q: 为什么「流处理只是更快的批处理」这句话有坑？
q_en: Why is 'streaming is just faster batch' a trap?
why: 流处理不是批处理提速,而是另一套运维模型:常驻集群、状态管理、checkpoint、背压、迟到/乱序处理都要长期维护,运营成本常被低估。上流前应确认新鲜度确实需要,并算上这份持续开销。
why_en: Streaming isn't sped-up batch but a different ops model — resident clusters, state, checkpointing, backpressure, late-event handling — whose operational cost is commonly underestimated.
options: 因为流处理其实比批处理更慢,延迟更高,所以根本不该拿它来支撑任何实时或近实时的特征
因为流是另一套运维模型:常驻+状态+checkpoint+背压+乱序处理,运营成本常被低估
因为流处理在任何引擎上都无法保证 exactly-once,只要用它数据就一定会重复或丢失
因为流处理只能做最简单的计数累加,算不了滑动窗口、聚合等任何带时间维度的特征
options_en: Because streaming is actually slower than batch with higher latency, so it should never back any real-time or near-real-time feature.
Because streaming is a different ops model — resident cluster + state + checkpoint + backpressure + out-of-order handling — whose operational cost is commonly underestimated.
Because streaming can't guarantee exactly-once on any engine, so using it always duplicates or drops data.
Because streaming can only do the simplest count accumulation and cannot compute sliding windows, aggregations, or any time-based feature.
optionExplanations: 流处理对实时特征更快而非更慢;坑不在速度,而在长期运维负担被低估。
对;流是另一套运营模型,状态/背压/乱序/checkpoint 都要长期养,成本别只算机器价。
Flink 等能提供 exactly-once,并非一定丢数据;把它说成必丢是误解。
流处理恰恰擅长窗口聚合(如滑动计数),说它只能简单计数不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Streaming is faster not slower for real-time features; the trap isn't speed but underestimated long-term ops burden.
Correct — streaming is a different ops model where state/backpressure/out-of-order/checkpointing need ongoing care, so don't price only the machines.
Engines like Flink offer exactly-once, so data isn't always lost; calling it guaranteed loss is a misconception.
Streaming excels at window aggregation like sliding counts, so 'only simple counts' is false.

termDefinitions.meaning: 下游处理不过来时向上游施加的流控,流管线需妥善处理以防崩溃。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backpressure is flow control applied upstream when downstream can't keep up, which stream pipelines must handle to avoid collapse.

scenario: 面试里你要为「用户 embedding 用日频批处理」这个选择给一句有说服力的理由,展示成本意识。
scenario_en: In an interview you must justify 'compute user embeddings with a daily batch' in one convincing line that shows cost awareness.
q: 为一个管线选择辩护时,一句好理由应该点名哪三件事？
q_en: When justifying a pipeline choice, a good one-liner should name which three things?
why: 好理由 = 特征名 + 新鲜度需求 + 成本含义,例如「用户 embedding 用日频批算,因为口味变化慢,省掉了常驻流处理的成本」。这三件套把选择绑到约束上,正是面试官想听的约束驱动推理。
why_en: A good justification names the feature, its freshness need, and the cost implication — e.g. 'user embeddings batch daily because taste shifts slowly, saving always-on streaming cost.'
tradeoff: 按新鲜度需求选档(有据可依) vs 无理由默认某范式(暴露成本意识缺失)
options: 点名:特征名 + 新鲜度需求 + 成本含义,把选择绑到约束上
点名:模型准确率 + 训练轮数 + 参数量
点名:用哪家云 + 机房位置 + 网络带宽
点名:团队规模 + 开发排期 + 汇报对象
options_en: Name the feature + its freshness need + the cost implication, tying the choice to constraints.
Name model accuracy + training epochs + parameter count.
Name which cloud + data-center location + network bandwidth.
Name team size + dev timeline + reporting chain.
whenOtherWins: 若该特征其实新鲜度敏感(分钟级欺诈),同样的三件套会把理由导向流处理而非批处理——三件套不变,结论随约束变。
whenOtherWins_en: If the feature is actually freshness-sensitive (minute-scale fraud), the same trio steers the justification to streaming instead of batch.
optionExplanations: 对;特征+新鲜度+成本三件套让选择有据可依,体现约束驱动推理,正中面试官下怀。
训练轮数/参数量是建模超参,回答不了「这条特征该用什么管线」的选型理由。
云厂商/机房/带宽是基建采购,不构成按新鲜度选管线的论据。
团队与排期是项目管理,与特征管线的技术选型理由无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the feature+freshness+cost trio grounds the choice in constraints, showing constraint-driven reasoning the interviewer wants.
Epochs/parameters are modeling hyperparameters and don't justify which pipeline a feature needs.
Cloud/location/bandwidth is infra procurement, not an argument for choosing a pipeline by freshness.
Team and timeline are project management, unrelated to the technical justification for a feature pipeline.

termDefinitions.term: constraint-driven reasoning / 约束驱动推理
termDefinitions.meaning: 先摆出新鲜度/延迟/成本约束,再让约束推出选型,而非默认某方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Constraint-driven reasoning states freshness/latency/cost constraints first and lets them dictate the choice rather than defaulting.
